node.why: Classification follows the destination map that already exists.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Classification uses the destination map already present for this product.
The agent writes its synthesis to the agent destination that map already names.
A person can open that result from the location the map already gives.

constraints: At most 6 grep calls and 15 read calls.

project.description: A milestone metric graph focused on basic evals and honest goals for the  AgentOS core loop, bridging multiple interfaces (Obsidian, Taskdog, Zed, Terminal) into a transparently simple 3-layer system (Visual, Memory, Skills).

blueprint.vision: Implement the 5-part spine of the Jev + Claude OS walkthrough: Three layers,  request routing, skill backbone, organized memory, and a shared interface.
blueprint.architecture_notes: Nodes represent behavioral milestones and evals rather than technical specs.  Focus on proving the core loop works from request -> routing -> skill execution -> memory write-back.
major_capabilities: Memory classification against the established destination map

nodes.title: Eval: Bridge accepts requests from multiple interfaces (Obsidian, Taskdog, Zed, Terminal)
milestones: A request sent from Obsidian is recorded once by the bridge.
The same request sent from a second client (Zed, Taskdog, or the terminal) is recorded by that same bridge.
Both submissions are routed to the same outcome.

nodes.title: Eval: Router enforces budget and escalation criteria to dynamically select the most cost-effective model/agent (logs decisions for Laya)
milestones: A simple lookup ('Bring up the morning brief') stays under the minimum budget threshold and executes as an instant action.
A generative request ('What was the biggest news?') triggers the fast-model budget criteria and returns a cheap, fast answer.
A complex request ('Write me an explainer') hits the escalation criteria, routes to a full agent, and logs the decision for Laya's shadow training.

nodes.title: Goal: Convert at least one manual conversational workflow into an automated, headless skill
milestones: One recurring workflow (a presence brief over social accounts, Taskdog, and daily notes) is documented so a human could follow it manually.
That same skill runs headlessly and writes its finished deliverable to the agent destination the existing map already names.
Running the skill a second time produces a new deliverable without requiring any code rewrites to the skill.

nodes.title: Goal: The shared interface displays deliverables (metrics, schedules) driven by the headless skills
milestones: The presence-brief deliverable is visible on Obsidian or a lean desktop app without opening the background run.
The metrics inside the deliverable, including social accounts and GitHub commits, are fully rendered and visible.
Asking a question about the deliverable from that display reads the persistent copy the skill wrote.
